bug_semantics: Authenticated stored XSS on invoice/bill detail timelines. An authenticated user stores HTML/JavaScript in their profile name (PATCH profile/{user}; User request only validates name as required|string; UpdateUser persists raw input). When that user creates or cancels a document, Create.php/Restore.php copy owner->name into $user_name and the Blade views interpolate it unescaped into trans('documents.slider.create'|cancel) replacements such as ':user created this :type on :date'. The date field is already a trusted HTML <span>, so the composed description is passed with {!! trans(...) !!} into x-show.accordion.head, which emits {!! $description !!}. Laravel trans() does not HTML-escape replacements, so another viewer of the document executes the stored name as HTML/JS.
flaw_origin: The first public write of this mechanism is d9c076457215c089cd221dbd4c822ce6a3bd021b (2022-06-01, 'akaunting 3.0 (the last dance)', author/committer Burak Civan), which added resources/views/components/documents/show/create.blade.php with description="{!! trans($description, ['user' => $document->owner->name, 'date' => $created_date]) !!}" plus resources/views/components/show/accordion/head.blade.php emitting {!! $description !!} and lang invoices.slider.create = ':user created this invoice on :date'. Immediate parent cead09f6d4fc9a1f589da7cdbff57f269a46ba00 has neither file; the pre-3.0 timeline used escaped {{ trans(...) }} without interpolating owner names. f15f8c68d812aa58a443e3c8c886a858dd588819 (akaunting 3.1) only refactored create.blade.php to $user_name and copied the same unescaped trans() pattern onto the cancel/restore path; that is not the first write.

reasoning: CVE-2026-11943 is a real published CWE-79 (CVE.org state PUBLISHED; GHSA not withdrawn). The attack is stored XSS: unsanitized profile name is interpolated into a translated HTML timeline sentence and rendered with Blade {!! !!} on invoice/bill show pages. The complete mechanism first appears in d9c076457215c089cd221dbd4c822ce6a3bd021b, which created create.blade.php with unescaped 'user' => $document->owner->name inside {!! trans(...) !!} and the accordion head sink {!! $description !!}. Direct parent-tree check shows those files absent at cead09f6d4fc9a1f589da7cdbff57f269a46ba00, and the older timeline escaped translations without owner names, so this is a first write rather than a move. The 3.0 commit is a large UI rewrite dumped through PR #2401; inspecting that PR and the brkcvn fork file history does not yield a finer public commit that wrote the vulnerable lines, so d9c076 is the smallest surviving public BIC (squash_decomposed=false). The 3.1 commit is a refactor of the create path plus a later copy onto restore/cancel, and is not the BIC. The BIC precedes affected 3.1.21 (ancestor of tags 3.0.0 through 3.2.2). AI attribution is taken only from the BIC commit object: human author/committer Burak Civan, no AI trailers or bot identity, therefore NOT_AI. The finding is unpatched: Fluid Attacks recorded no vendor patch, CVE lists no fixed version, and the same sinks remain at 3.2.2 and HEAD with no post-disclosure edits.

potential_fix.approach: HTML-escape the user-controlled name before translation, e.g. set $this->user_name = e($this->document->owner->name) in Create.php and Restore.php (and the same for send/receive timeline siblings), leaving only the trusted date <span> unescaped; alternatively pass 'user' => e($user_name) in create.blade.php and restore.blade.php. Do not rely on {!! $description !!} in accordion/head.blade.php to stay raw for attacker data.
potential_fix.rationale: Laravel trans() performs unescaped placeholder replacement, and accordion/head.blade.php prints the result with {!! !!} so that the date <span> renders. Encoding the name closes the XSS while preserving the intended date markup. Input strip_tags on profile name is defense-in-depth only and would not fix other encoded-output paths.
